counterexample: Take n = 4 and G = triangle on {a,b,c} plus an isolated vertex d, with the 3 cycle edges (|C| = 3) and 0 remaining edges, i.e. n-1 = 3 edges total. The step's edge accounting already fails in general (the n-1-|C| leftover edges need not lie inside the remaining vertex set; they may join the cycle to other vertices, as in the 'paw' graph: triangle a,b,c plus edge c-d, n = 4, edges = 3). And the step's key claim is outright impossible here: the subgraph on the n-|C| = 1 remaining vertex has exactly 1 connected component, yet the proof asserts it must have at least |C|+1 = 4 components. A graph on 1 vertex cannot have 4 components.
reasoning_summary: Step 0001 states the claim (G on n vertices with n-1 edges is connected iff acyclic); 0002 is blank. Step 0003 attempts the contrapositive of 'connected implies acyclic': it assumes a cycle C using |C| vertices and |C| edges, says n-|C| vertices and n-1-|C| edges remain, and then asserts 'this subgraph must contain at least |C|+1 connected components'. Two things break here. (a) The edge bookkeeping is invalid: the n-1-|C| non-cycle edges need not be edges of the induced subgraph on the remaining n-|C| vertices; they may have one or both endpoints on the cycle, so no conclusion about that subgraph's edge count follows. (b) The component bound is false and in fact often numerically impossible: a graph on n-|C| vertices has at most n-|C| components, and the only bound the counting gives is (#vertices) - (#edges) = (n-|C|) - (n-1-|C|) = 1 component, not |C|+1. Whenever n-|C| < |C|+1 (e.g. a triangle plus one extra vertex, n=4, |C|=3) the asserted bound cannot hold. Since the whole 'only if' direction rests on this bound to conclude more than one component, the step is unjustified and false as written, so I stop here. (The conclusion of the theorem itself is true — a connected graph on n vertices with n-1 edges is a tree — but this argument does not establish it. For completeness, step 0005 is also invalid: it merely exhibits one acyclic connected graph, a path, rather than showing every acyclic graph with n vertices and n-1 edges is connected.)
